newsitem.title: USA: Gilead notes Vistide toxicity in 2 patients.
newsitem.headline: Gilead notes Vistide toxicity in 2 patients.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc Vice President Linda Hamilton said doctors reported nephrotoxicity, or renal impairment in two of over 2,000 patients treated with its Vistide drug in clinical tests and after the drug's approval in June.
Concerns that Vistide, used to treat blindness in AIDS patients, is showing signs of toxicity sent shares of the drug company down three to 25-3/4 by mid-afternoon on Tuesday.

The company began telling doctors of the toxicity earlier this week at the Interscience conference on chemotherapy and antimicrobial agents. Hamilton said Gilead has been reminding physicians to be careful when choosing patients for Vistide.

Analysts speculated that in the two nephrotoxicity cases resulting from Vistide, which treats cytomegalovirus retinitis in AIDS patients, the drug was administered to patients who were likely too sick to receive it safely.
They said the news gave short-term investors a reason to sell, noting the stock has risen rapidly to 29-3/4 on Friday from 17-3/8 on Aug. 6.

"When a stock has had a run up, it reaches a point with some resistance," said Stephen Sabba, an analyst with Sturza's Institutional Research. He said Gilead's proactive stance toward telling physicians about the two cases is encouraging.
